newsitem.title: USA: Spilled horse lotion makes 50 postal workers ill.
newsitem.headline: Spilled horse lotion makes 50 postal workers ill.

text.p: A bottle of a chemical used to treat horses broke open at a post office branch on Tuesday, sending more than 50 workers to hospitals with such symptoms as burning throats and nausea, authorities said.
None of the injuries from the spill of several ounces of concentrated synthetic mustard oil, used in a diluted form by veterinarians to treat horses' injured tendons, was deemed serious.

But several workers quickly stripped down to their underwear in a parking lot to wash the stinging chemical off their bodies. A pair of strategically parked fire trucks shielded the impromptu bathers from onlookers.

A 20-ounce bottle of the liquid broke open, although it had been protected by cardboard and plastic bubble wrap, sending 55 postal workers and two firemen to the hospital complaining of nausea, dizziness, irritated skin, sore throats and an odd taste in their mouths, U.S. Postal Inspector P.J. Farmer said.
A hazardous substance team was sent to the post office's Southport branch to clean up the liquid, which was being mailed by a local stable to a Kentucky horse farm, Farmer said.
